AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I think the answer is 1, which means YTA (You're The Asshole). As a parent, it's natural to want to visit and connect with your son, especially since he's been ignoring you. However, showing up unannounced at his apartment can be seen as an overstep of boundaries. Your son is 19, living in a different city, and trying to establish his independence. By not respecting his wishes for space and not calling ahead, you may have made him feel like you're not trusting him to manage his own life. It's also possible that your son is indeed busy with studies and other responsibilities, and your frequent calls may have been feeling overwhelming or suffocating to him. His request for space and your decision to show up anyway may have been perceived as dismissive of his needs and boundaries. Additionally, your comment about the apartment needing a good clean, although likely made in jest, may have come across as judgmental or critical. This could have added to your son's annoyance and feeling of being lectured or mothered. It's essential to respect your son's autonomy and boundaries, even if it's challenging as a parent. Instead of showing up unannounced, you could try having an open and honest conversation with him about your concerns and feelings. This might help you better understand his perspective and find a mutually respectful way to stay connected.
